headline: ASX closes up 0.6% as Pilbara Minerals surges 4% and Microsoft's AI cloud boom lifts US holdings — six months of war in Iran reshaping global energy markets.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Strong session today on the ASX — PLS jumped 4.1%, likely benefiting from broader positive sentiment around lithium and materials as the ASX 200 climbed. No specific company news today, but it's a welcome bounce for a stock still sitting 20% below your buy-in price.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft surged last night after blowout Q4 results showed AI-powered cloud revenue well ahead of expectations. The Simply Wall Street note flagged a 6.3% post-earnings jump, and the stock continues to hold those gains — the AI story here is very real and still has legs.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google rose last night alongside Microsoft as the broader market rewarded big tech's AI momentum. No specific Google news today, but it's riding the same AI cloud wave that lifted MSFT.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up last night after Rockstar Games released an extended look at GTA VI, stoking fresh excitement about the game's release. Variety and Good Morning America both covered it heavily — this is the catalyst the stock has been waiting for.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Nudged up slightly today on the ASX, tracking the general positive AI sentiment. Still sitting 13.6% below your invested amount — patience required, but the AI theme globally remains very active.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A small positive session today on the ASX. Emerging markets remain under some pressure from ongoing Middle East conflict and its economic ripple effects, particularly in developing nations.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Quiet but positive session today. VDHG's diversified mix of global and Australian shares meant it captured some of the ASX's 0.6% gain without any dramatic moves.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: A small gain today on the ASX — the US market data baked into VTS reflects last night's mixed session on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 dipped slightly but big tech held firm.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — big bounce today but still deep in the red
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.1% today, which is great to see, but you're still down about 20% on this position ($30.71 AUD). No specific news drove today's move — it looks like general ASX materials strength. The long-term thesis depends on lithium demand recovering as EV adoption grows. Nothing broken here structurally, so sit tight and let it ride.

watch_today.title: MSFT — AI cloud boom is the real deal
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's Q4 results last night showed AI-fuelled cloud revenue beating expectations, sending the stock up 6.3% on earnings and it's held those gains. You're now up nearly 16% on your MSFT position ($62 AUD profit). The long-term AI story here is genuinely strong. No reason to sell — if anything, dips are worth adding to.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI extended preview drops, stock up
watch_today.detail: Rockstar released an extended look at Grand Theft Auto VI last night and it sent Take-Two's stock up 1% — but the real payoff comes when the game actually launches. Your TTWO position is only just above water (+1.4%, ~$9 AUD). The GTA VI hype cycle is building. This is a long-term hold — the game release will be the real catalyst.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still underwater, but theme is very active
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF is down 13.6% overall ($40.52 AUD in the red) despite today's tiny nudge up. The AI sector globally is buzzing — OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia CEOs are speaking at a G20 tech summit, and AI cyberattack warnings are keeping the sector in the news. This is a long-term theme play — no reason to exit, just takes time.

watch_today.title: RBA rate outlook shifting — banks backflip on rate call
watch_today.detail: Major Australian banks have reversed their Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) interest rate forecasts, with the RBA itself flagging ongoing inflation jitters. This matters for your ASX holdings — if rates stay higher for longer, it can weigh on growth stocks and property. Worth watching heading into the next RBA meeting.

watch_today.title: Gold drops 1.7% — safe haven selling as risk appetite returns
watch_today.detail: Gold fell sharply last night to US$4,530/oz, down 1.7%. This isn't in your portfolio directly but signals that markets are in a 'risk-on' mood — which is generally good for your growth-oriented holdings like MSFT, GOOG and GXAI.AX.

world.summary: The Middle East conflict continues to dominate global news at the six-month mark, reshaping energy markets and causing economic pain across developing nations. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is making headlines for targeting government officials and fighting court orders on voting rules.

stories.title: Six months of war in Iran: what's changed and what it means
stories.why_it_matters: Six months into the conflict involving Iran, Reuters has mapped out the major consequences — from a reshaping of oil supply routes, to tightened US sanctions, to rising poverty in countries that trade heavily with Iran. For everyday Australians, the key effect is on energy prices: oil is now sitting around US$83/barrel, and any further escalation could push petrol prices higher. Iran is lashing out publicly at US sanctions as its economy deteriorates at home.

stories.title: Middle East conflict creates energy winners and losers
stories.why_it_matters: Bloomberg reports that the ongoing Middle East war is creating a split in global energy markets — some producers (like Gulf states not involved in the fighting) are cashing in on higher oil prices, while others are being squeezed out of supply chains. For investors, this means energy stocks and oil prices remain volatile and geopolitically sensitive. Australia, as a major LNG exporter, could see some indirect benefit if energy prices stay elevated.

stories.title: World Bank warns of job losses and rising poverty in Bangladesh from Middle East fallout
stories.why_it_matters: The World Bank is warning that the ripple effects of the Middle East war are hitting Bangladesh hard, with job losses expected in garment and export industries and a rise in poverty feared. This is a reminder that conflicts don't stay contained — they push up global shipping costs, disrupt supply chains, and squeeze the world's most vulnerable economies. It also adds pressure on emerging market investments like VGE.AX, which has exposure to South and Southeast Asian economies.

stories.title: Trump administration targets James Comey and others — list released
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has published a list of individuals it is targeting, including former FBI Director James Comey. This is part of a broader pattern of the administration using government power to go after perceived political opponents. It's causing significant concern among legal observers about the independence of US institutions — something that can affect market confidence in US stability over the medium term.

stories.title: Trump administration appeals court order freezing mail-in voting rule
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is appealing a federal court order that blocked its new rules restricting mail-in voting. This is an ongoing legal battle over voting access ahead of the next election cycle. Courts have repeatedly paused the administration's voting restrictions, but the fight continues — the outcome will have major implications for how Americans vote and which communities have easiest access to the ballot.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 0.6% at 9,092. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 edged down 0.25% and the NASDAQ slipped 0.52% — but that mild pullback masked strong individual performances from big tech names like Microsoft and Google. Gold sold off sharply (-1.7%), while oil barely moved. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly against the US dollar.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — up 0.6%, materials and tech helping lead the way.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a modest dip — but big tech held up well individually.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night — slight pullback on the index, though MSFT and GOOG both rose on their own merits.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat — Middle East tensions keeping a floor under prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Sharp drop last night — markets in 'risk-on' mode, reducing demand for safe-haven assets.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar slipped slightly — worth watching as a softer AUD boosts the value of your US holdings when converted back.

politics.summary: Australian domestic focus is squarely on interest rates, with major banks reversing their RBA forecasts and the Reserve Bank flagging continued inflation concerns. There's no sign of rate cuts coming soon.

stories.title: Major banks backflip on RBA rate cut call
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's major banks — which had been tipping rate cuts from the Reserve Bank of Australia — have now reversed those forecasts. That means mortgage holders and borrowers should not expect relief soon. For investors, higher-for-longer rates can weigh on growth stocks and property values, but they also signal that the economy is still running warm enough to keep inflation sticky. The RBA itself has confirmed it remains 'jittery' about inflation risks.

stories.title: Reserve Bank of Australia remains jittery about inflation risks
stories.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal reports that the RBA is still worried about inflation not coming down fast enough, despite interest rates already being at elevated levels. The RBA's concern is that wage growth and services inflation (think haircuts, rent, restaurants) are proving stubborn. For everyday Australians, this means rates are likely to stay higher for longer, keeping mortgage repayments elevated going into the summer.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the big theme this week — from cybersecurity warnings to medical devices to synthetic biology. There's also a practical consumer angle with multi-AI subscription bundles making it easier and cheaper to access all the major AI chatbots in one place.

stories.title: 100 companies including OpenAI and Anthropic warn of escalating AI cyberattacks
stories.why_it_matters: A coalition of 100 major tech companies — including OpenAI and Anthropic — have jointly warned that AI-powered cyberattacks are escalating rapidly. The concern is that criminals and state actors are using AI tools to make hacking faster, smarter, and harder to detect. This is pushing cybersecurity stocks into focus and signals that AI safety and security will be a major regulatory battleground over the next few years. For investors, cybersecurity ETFs and companies may benefit.

stories.title: OpenAI and Nvidia CEOs to speak at tech-focused G20 meeting
stories.why_it_matters: The CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman) and Nvidia (Jensen Huang) are heading to a G20 tech summit, signalling that AI has become a top-tier geopolitical and economic issue — not just a tech industry conversation. Governments are increasingly looking to shape global AI rules, and having the heads of the world's most powerful AI companies at the table could influence international standards. This is relevant to holdings like MSFT and GOOG, which operate in a landscape increasingly shaped by government AI policy.

stories.title: FDA seeks public input on regulating AI medical devices
stories.why_it_matters: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is asking for public comment on how to regulate AI tools used in healthcare — things like AI that reads medical scans, diagnoses conditions, or recommends treatments. This is a big deal because AI is moving fast in medicine but the rules haven't caught up. How the FDA ultimately decides to regulate this will shape billions of dollars in investment and affect companies like Google (which has major AI health projects) and Microsoft (which has a large healthcare AI division).

stories.title: One subscription to rule them all: GPT, Claude, Gemini and more for ~$30-80
stories.why_it_matters: A handful of services are now offering single subscriptions that give you access to ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google) and other AI chatbots all in one place — for a one-off payment of around $30-$80 USD. This is a practical development for anyone who wants to try different AI tools without paying $20-$30/month for each separately. It also signals that the AI chatbot market is maturing and becoming more commoditised, which could affect how these platforms compete on price and features going forward.

sport.summary: NRL Round 26 is effectively done and dusted, with the top eight now locked in. Big results this weekend include the Storm's demolition of the Broncos at Suncorp, the Rabbitohs booking their finals spot, and the Dolphins beating the Roosters. The AFL wildcard round is also stirring controversy.

stories.title: NRL top eight locked in — Storm destroy Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp
stories.why_it_matters: The Melbourne Storm put on a clinic at Suncorp Stadium, handing the Brisbane Broncos a 46-20 thrashing on Thursday night. The result confirms the NRL's top eight are now locked in for the finals. The Wests Tigers are officially out of contention, having also lost 24-10 to the Cowboys in Townsville. Fox Sports reported a 'horror moment' for the Tigers sealed their fate.

stories.title: Knights prop sent off for 'savage' hit that knocked out young rival
stories.why_it_matters: In the Warriors vs Knights match (Warriors won 46-32), a Newcastle Knights prop was sent off for a 'savage' high hit that knocked out a young Warriors player. The incident is expected to attract a lengthy suspension at the judiciary and has reignited the debate around player safety and head contact in the NRL. It's a black mark on what was otherwise a high-scoring, entertaining game.

stories.title: Rabbitohs lock in finals spot with touching Arrow tribute and Latrell's return
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney Rabbitohs beat the Gold Coast Titans 42-22 at Cbus Super Stadium to lock in their finals spot. The game featured a moving tribute to the late David Arrow, and star fullback Latrell Mitchell returned from injury in timely fashion. The Dolphins also had a great weekend, beating the Roosters 26-12 at Allianz Stadium to strengthen their own finals position.

stories.title: AFL wildcard round slammed as fans raise retirement concerns
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's wildcard round is drawing criticism on two fronts: fans are unhappy that the league 'buried' a key announcement rather than giving it proper attention, and a double retirement during the wildcard weekend has prompted debate about whether the format respects players' career endings. Carlton kept their season alive with a wildcard win, but the AFL's handling of the round has left many supporters frustrated.
